_doc: Concept map for onevisit/search.py: the ID card vocabulary in Italian and in the languages people write in (English, Spanish, French, Arabic, Chinese, Ukrainian/Russian, Bengali).
Each concept becomes one search term. A passage gets it when one of its 'phrases' occurs in the passage (or its heading);
a query gets it when one of its 'phrases' or 'query_only' entries occurs in the query. So 'I lost my ID card', 'perdí mi DNI'
and 'ho perso la carta d'identità' all search for the same two concepts and find the same Italian passages.
Matching: accents removed, lower case, apostrophes and hyphens split words ('all'estero' = 'all estero', 'check-in' = 'check in').
Latin-script phrases match whole words in sequence; a word ending in '*' matches any word that starts with it ('smarri*').

Arabic, Cyrillic and Bengali phrases match at the start of a word (Arabic prefixes 'و ب ل ف ك ال' allowed: 'للأجانب' finds 'أجانب'), so a stem finds its endings ('дитин' finds дитина, дитини, дитиною) but not the middle of another word ('форм' is not in 'інформація'). A phrase of four letters or fewer must be (almost) the whole word: Arabic pronoun endings, up to three letters of Cyrillic or Bengali endings. Chinese phrases match as substrings (no spaces between words).
'query_only' holds words that are common in the pages with another meaning (Italian 'dove' is also 'where' in a relative clause).
'query_regex' (optional) are regular expressions on the folded query, for what words can't list: an age of 70 or more is 'elderly', under 18 'minor'.

'not' (optional) lists phrases inside which the concept's words mean something else: 'ho subito un furto' is not urgent, 'I arrived in Milan' is not a delivery. A match of the concept inside a 'not' phrase is dropped, in pages and in queries.

'distinct': true marks a concept that names another thing than the card itself (the PIN codes, the digital credentials, organ donation, the residence permit...). A section whose heading is about it ranks lower when the question doesn't mention it: 'I lost my ID card' is not 'I lost my PIN'.

'off_topic': true marks a concept of questions that are not about any procedure (the weather, small talk, a restaurant): a query that asks it and not the service's own subject gets no confident answer (reason 'off_topic'). Its words are 'query_only'.
Never put a fact here: this file only says which words mean the same thing. Reviewed by a person like any other data file.

'means_for' (optional) lists concepts for which this other document is only the means (SPID to book an appointment or to go online): a question with one of them is about the service, not about the other document.

'asks_other_document': true marks a concept of questions that ask to obtain or renew another document ('fare il passaporto all'anagrafe'): such a question is about that document even when it also names the ID card. Its weight is 0: it only gates, it never ranks.

'frame': true marks a concept that says how a question is asked (what to bring, where, when, is it mandatory, can I apply) more than what it is about: a passage needs the question's other concepts to be a confident answer, not these.

'unanswered_topic': true marks a concept no saved page answers (parking near an office, bringing a pet): a question that asks it gets the honest 'the pages don't say' (reason 'unknown_words'), whatever generic word (office, anagrafe) it shares with the pages.

'situation': true marks the person's situation or why the card is needed (lost, stolen, damaged, expired, renewal; a minor, a student, a foreign resident): a passage that holds the rest of the question ('quanto costa rifarla se l'ho persa?': the fee) answers it without naming the situation; a question about the situation alone needs it.

how long is the card valid

abbreviations._doc: Chat shorthand read as the word it stands for, in queries only.

_doc: How words of the scripts the pages are not written in (Arabic, Chinese, Cyrillic, Bengali) are read.
arabic_prefixes / arabic_suffixes: what may stand before or after an Arabic phrase in the same word (conjunction, preposition, article; possessive pronouns).
function_words, function_chars (Chinese) and ignored_word_starts (Milan, Italy, Italian): words that say nothing about a question's topic.
A question word of these scripts that no concept reads and that is not listed here lowers the search's confidence: the pages can only be reached through the concepts.
